item.title: Software Engineering at Google, Ch 11: Testing Overview
item.description: Why did Google stop trusting smart engineers alone to keep bugs out? In this deep dive on Chapter 11 of Software Engineering at Google (Winters, Manshreck & Wright; chapter by Adam Bender), we follow the Google Web Server's turnaround from a mostly-rolled-back release process to a test-every-change culture, then unpack the chapter's toolkit: test size versus scope, hermetic and flaky tests, the 80/15/5 test pyramid and its ice-cream-cone and hourglass antipatterns, the Beyoncé Rule, why code coverage misleads, and how bathroom flyers and a five-level certification ladder changed engineering habits without a leadership mandate. Built from an IntuiBloom knowledge graph. Explore the IntuiBloom graph: https://www.IntuiBloom.com/share/zpspbstUa4zxmLl41nB3z9I1uDhAQG5TT7gEptFsZ1s=
